scope: Prioritized acquisition shortlist for Atlas Expert v1. Focus on ~700k expert records across Software Engineering, AI/ML, Mathematics, System Engineering, and Science.
constraints: Permissive or Atlas-approved licenses only unless explicitly reviewed.
No bulk ingestion of restricted/RAIL/proprietary datasets without subsetting plan.
E3 sources are accepted for signal, not volume.
All sources must pass: license check -> quality filter -> difficulty scoring -> expert layer.

sources.name: SWE-bench verified
sources.notes: Gold patches verified by FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS. Strong issue-to-patch expert signal.

sources.name: StackExchange Code XML dumps
sources.notes: Voted Q&A. Keep accepted/high-score answers only. Requires attribution + PII stripping.

sources.name: GitHub issue-to-solution pairs
sources.notes: Needs source discovery: preferred repos with permissive issue/PR licensing or public-domain contributions.

sources.name: Code review expert examples
sources.notes: Preferred sources: public review datasets, Mozilla/Google style guides + review traces, or permissive review exports.

sources.name: System design Q&A
sources.notes: Preferred sources: curated system design Q&A with verified answers, or doc-derived instruction from architecture references.

sources.name: ArXiv cs.LG / cs.CL / cs.AI / stat.ML
sources.notes: Tier-1 academic source. Convert well-sourced sections to expert Q&A; cite arXiv ID.

sources.name: Open-Platypus
sources.notes: Expert-curated science/math/code. Verify factual claims; some GPT-4 generated content possible.

sources.name: ML textbook derivations and explanations
sources.notes: Preferred sources: open ML textbooks, course notes, lecture-derived Q&A with permissive license.

sources.name: Experiment analysis and paper explanation pairs
sources.notes: Preferred sources: paper-explanation datasets, public leaderboard analysis, or human-authored research reviews.

sources.name: AIME / AMC / competition math problems
sources.notes: Classic frontier math. Verify redistribution rights before ingestion.

sources.name: OpenMathInstruct-2
sources.notes: Large math instruction dataset. Verify gating status and MIT license on download.

sources.name: Proof-Pile / mathematical documents corpus
sources.notes: Preferred sources: openly licensed proof corpora, arxiv math subsets, or textbook-derived Q&A.

sources.name: University-level math reasoning problems
sources.notes: Preferred sources: course exams, open coursework, or curated problem sets with verified solutions.

sources.name: Linux man-pages + kernel documentation
sources.notes: Tier-1 authoritative. Convert to Q/A via templates; flag GFDL subsections.

sources.name: Kubernetes official documentation
sources.notes: Pin doc version. Convert to expert instruction pairs.

sources.name: Docker official documentation
sources.notes: Stable container-domain expert signal.

sources.name: Arch Wiki
sources.notes: Strong practical systems depth. Requires attribution + share-alike tracking.

sources.name: Red Hat / Fedora Documentation
sources.notes: Enterprise-grade system administration content.

sources.name: StackExchange Systems dumps
sources.notes: Real troubleshooting Q&A. Filter high-score posts only; strip PII.

sources.name: Distributed systems papers and notes
sources.notes: Preferred sources: MIT 6.824-style notes, open distributed-systems textbooks, or paper-derived Q&A.

sources.name: GSM8K
sources.notes: Gold chain-of-thought math. Reserve test split for evaluation.

sources.name: MMLU STEM subset
sources.notes: Broad science/engineering knowledge. Convert MC to open-form for SFT only.

sources.name: Hendrycks MATH
sources.notes: Competition-level math with verified solutions.

sources.name: OpenWebMath
sources.notes: Math-dense web corpus. Filter and convert to expert instruction pairs.

sources.name: Graduate science textbook excerpts
sources.notes: Preferred sources: openly licensed physics/chemistry/biology textbooks or lecture notes with redistribution rights.

note: Estimates above include both confirmed accepted sources and placeholder candidate targets. Human-supplied sources must be discovered and licensed before ingestion.
